Sam: Heads-up — noticed a tail latency regression after the kernel-selector change this morning. 95p latency up ~30% on p3-small tests.
Leila: Ugh. Which kernel path got chosen more often?
Sam: The new matmul-tiling kernel is winning for mid-seq lengths (128-512) now. Perf profiler shows more workspace alloc churn.
Matt: I saw an increase in pad amplification in batcher metrics too — average pad/token ratio jumped from 1.18 -> 1.45 for that workload.
Dina: Could be interaction with KV cache. When prefix hits are lower we see wider seq variance so batching pads more. Any KV hit-rate diffs?
Jun: KV hit-rate looks flat in tracing but we have 12% more partial prefix miss cases after the kernel change. Might be timing shift in request ordering.
Sam: Attached quick trace dump:
```
# simplified trace
batch_id=9834 seqs=[64, 200, 512, 128]
selected_kernel=matmul-tiling
workspace_requested=4.2GB
workspace_allocated=6GB  # due to slab rounding + pad
kv_cache_miss=2
```
Leila: That workspace delta (+1.8GB) matches the slab coalesce heuristic hitting next power-of-two. Our allocator watermark bumped the slab size.
Matt: We should be careful: kernel tiling requires extra temporary buffers for blocked GEMM; that explains the larger per-batch high-water mark.
Dina: Can we reproduce with a tight repro? I can run a debug build with alloc telemetry.
Jun: I started one against the same synthetic load — will share flamegraphs.
ops-bot: CI job batch-regress-210987 triggered by @Sam — run id `ci-7021` — logs: https://ci/redwood/ci-7021
Sam: Quick perf snippet from `ci-7021` (summary):
- avg tokens/sec: down 12%
- 95p latency: up 31%
- avg pad_ratio: 1.46
- slab_waste_est: 1.6GB per-gpu
Leila: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) force fallback to old kernel for p95-critical routes; 2) lower slab rounding threshold for tiling kernel; 3) add per-seq pad cap to batcher to limit single-seq blowouts. Thoughts?
Matt: +1 for kernel fallback as hotfix. Lowering slab rounding needs careful perf testing — might drop throughput.
Dina: Per-seq cap seems low-risk and could cut pad waste quickly. We should pick a cap like 1.5x median seq for a short window.
Jun: Also consider eager buffer reuse across batch turns — reuse temporary tiling buffers when shapes match. That reduces alloc churn.
Sam: Action items:
- Sam: open rollback PR to prefer old-kernel on routes/benchmarks (in flight)
- Dina: run debug alloc build with `ALLOC_TELEMETRY=1` and upload flamegraphs (ETA 2h)
- Jun: prototype reuse cache for tiling temporaries (WIP)
- Leila: run simulation of per-seq cap 1.5x on production trace (ETA 4h)
Matt: I'll own monitoring alerts and update the SLO dashboard if p95 stays high.
Dina: Repro notes: use command `./run_batcher_test --seed 42 --trace ./prod_2026-03-17.json --kernel matmul-tiling` to hit the case.
Sam: FYI, KV team: if you see any request reordering that could change prefix alignment let us know — seems correlated.
Jun: Early flamegraph shows heavy time in `alloc_temp_block` and `slab_coalesce` for tiling path. Sharing link in thread once uploaded.
Matt: If fallback reduces latency we can do canary rollback next hour.
Leila: Also add a quick metric: slab_alloc_delta per-batch to make this visible in console.
Sam: Thanks — keeping this thread as the single source-of-truth. Ping me on @sam for urgent updates. :thumbsup:
